blocks.x: Who says the golden age of prestige TV is over? Not anyone watching last night’s broadcast of the 78th Emmy Awards, that’s for certain. As the creators of Widow’s Bay, The Pitt, Pluribus, The Gilded Age, Slow Horses, and Hacks picked up their statuettes last night, it underscored just how strong the 2026 lineup has been so far.

The red-carpet styling was no less satisfying. While previous years have been marked by a game of brinksmanship among Hollywood’s elite to outdo each other with ever-freakier getups, this award season kicked off with remarkable restraint. Yes, there were some big swings courtesy of Alan Cumming and Colman Domingo—a man who seems incapable of looking bad in anything—but most of the night’s best looks showed you don’t need to reinvent black-tie to make it look fresh. From wide trousers to quirky neckwear to the right brooch, red carpet excellence is all in the details. Here are our favorites.

There are no fancy bells and whistles here, no wacky designer flourishes or weirdo, fresh-off-the-runway deep cuts. All that’s here is The Pitt star Noah Wyle looking every bit the leading man in an almost-gray evening jacket and just-right black trousers. On a night when Hollywood’s flashiest dressers are encouraged to really go for it, keeping it simple is a swerve in and of itself.

The red-carpet styling was no less satisfying. While previous years have been marked by a game of brinksmanship among Hollywood’s elite to outdo each other with ever-freakier getups, this award season kicked off with remarkable restraint. Yes, there were some big swings courtesy of Alan Cumming and Colman Domingo—a man who seems incapable of looking bad in anything—but most of the night’s best looks showed you don’t need to reinvent black-tie to make it look fresh. From wide trousers to quirky neckwear to the right brooch, red carpet excellence is all in the details. Here are our favorites.

11. Noah Wyle in Brunello Cucinelli

There are no fancy bells and whistles here, no wacky designer flourishes or weirdo, fresh-off-the-runway deep cuts. All that’s here is The Pitt star Noah Wyle looking every bit the leading man in an almost-gray evening jacket and just-right black trousers. On a night when Hollywood’s flashiest dressers are encouraged to really go for it, keeping it simple is a swerve in and of itself.

Noah Wyle in Brunello Cucinelli

Monica Schipper/Getty Images

10. Matthew Rhys in Thom Browne

Rhys made history last night as the first actor to win two lead acting Emmys in a single night—for his roles in Widow’s Bay and The Beast in Me—and he turned to arguably the modern Hollywood red-carpet standard bearer for his ensemble: Thom Browne. Rather than showing out in one of Browne’s zingier kilts or tweeds, the Welshman opted for a classic black three-piece in the designer’s signature shrunken cut. All the better to let his dual hardware really shine.

Matthew Rhys in Thom Browne

Kevin Mazur/Getty Images

9. Kingston Rumi Southwick

Given that he’s just 18 years old, we don’t blame Widow’s Bay star Southwick for wanting to break from tradition and show out with his Emmys look. What landed him on this list, though, is the admirable restraint he showed in doing so: some silvery chain embroidery on his cuffs and down his seams; a brooch in place of a bow-tie; a simple black scarf draped around his neck; the slightest of flares in his trousers. Beyond all that, this is just a nicely cut, nicely executed tuxedo. Well done, young man.

Kingston Rumi Southwick

Gilbert Flores/Getty Images

8. Oscar Isaac in Celine

Beef star Oscar Isaac is a man of poignant subtleties, on the screen and off. His heel turn as beleaguered country-club manager Joshua Martín in the second season of the hit Netflix show was deliciously easy to root against, but his outfit at last night’s Emmy Awards might just be the redemption arc he deserves. Come for the slightly boxy jacket, stay for the relaxed trousers puddling ever-so-elegantly over his shoes. No beef on our end, folks.

Oscar Isaac in Celine

Monica Schipper/Getty Images

7. Paul Anthony Kelly in Louis Vuitton

Instead, the Love Story star opted for a look that felt exactly like the kind of thing the ’90s menswear icon might have worn. Equal parts traditional and of-the-moment, the look balances a conservative cut with expressive details like an oversized velvet bowtie and a clutch of tasteful gold jewelry.

Paul Anthony Kelly in Louis Vuitton

Amy Sussman/Getty Images

6. Matty Matheson in Harry Rosen

Of all the words one might use to describe the Canadian celebrity chef-turned-actor, understated isn’t among them. Still, Matheson, nominated for his role as executive producer on The Bear, nailed the assignment with an elevated black-tie look that felt only a little zany. His teeny-tiny batwing bowtie and cat-eye shades did most of the work, with an added dash of fun courtesy of his cummerbund and spats. As always, impeccable fit is the secret to making it work.

Matty Matheson in Harry Rosen

Kevin Mazur/Getty Images

5. Jason Segel in Isaia

Staring down the tail-end of wedding season and still haven’t figured out how your tuxedo should fit? You’re in luck: Last night, Jason Segel showed us all exactly how to black-tie like the second coming of ’80s-era Harrison Ford. (His Shrinking co-star and de facto work wife hit the red carpet with his actual wife, Calista Flockhart.) Just pull this picture up the next time you bring a tux to the tailor, and let the sublime, no-nonsense proportions on display here do the talking.

Jason Segel in Isaia

Kevin Mazur/Getty Images

4. Adam Brody in Prada

Now this is how you age gracefully as a former teen heartthrob, folks. Brody’s Prada rig accentuates his lean physique beautifully while balancing rakish ’70s swagger (teensy silk scarf and wide peak lapels) with enduring screen-idol appeal (rich navy wool and glossy black boots).

LOS ANGELES, CALIFORNIA - SEPTEMBER 14: Adam Brody attends the 78th Primetime Emmy Awards at Peacock Theater on September 14, 2026 in Los Angeles, California. (Photo by John Shearer/WireImage)John Shearer

3. Lee Sung Jin in Canali

Over the last few years, Beef creator Lee Sung Jin has emerged as one of the dapperest behind-the-camera talents in Hollywood, freaking it on red carpets in everything from Margiela Tabis to exaggerated shoulder pads. Here, though, he kept things relatively traditional in an impeccably tailored tux with all the minor details—from the size of his glasses to the shape of his shawl lapels to the droop of his bow tie—as tastefully appointed as can be.

Lee Sung Jin in Canali

Michael Buckner/Getty Images

2. Colman Domingo in Valentino

All hail Colman Domingo, king of the red carpet, who takes more big swings than Barry Bonds and never seems to miss. Nominated this year for his roles in Euphoria and The Four Seasons, the global ambassador for Maison Valentino has access to the kind of wardrobe menswear nerds dream of, and—as this custom Nehru jacket/sash combo proves—he takes full advantage. Few people could pull off any part of this outfit, and he makes it look effortless.

Colman Domingo in Valentino

Christopher Polk/Getty Images
